title: pipe and partial
description:
Write two helpers that build functions from functions:

- `pipe(...)` returns a function that passes its argument through each given function in turn, left to right; with no functions it returns its argument unchanged. Only the **first** result of each function is passed on.
- `partial(fn, ...)` returns a function that calls `fn` with the fixed arguments followed by the new ones. `nil` arguments (fixed or new) must stay in their places.

```lua
local f = pipe(function(x) return x + 1 end, function(x) return x * 10 end)
f(2)                                  --> 30
local hi = partial(string.format, "%s, %s!")
hi("Hello", "Ada")                    --> Hello, Ada!
```
hints: Wrapping a call in brackets, `(fns[i](x))`, keeps only its first result (lesson 8.02).
`table.pack(...)` stores the number of values in `n`; use it (not `#`) when copying and in `table.unpack(args, 1, count)`, so `nil`s are not lost.
unitTests:
test("pipe runs left to right", function()
    local f = pipe(function(x) return x + 1 end, function(x) return x * 10 end)
    check_eq(f(2), 30)
    check_eq(pipe()(7), 7)
end)

test("pipe passes only the first result on", function()
    local f = pipe(function(s) return s:gsub("a", "o") end, function(s, extra) return s .. tostring(extra) end)
    check_eq(f("banana"), "bonononil")
end)

test("partial fixes the first arguments", function()
    local hi = partial(string.format, "%s, %s!")
    check_eq(hi("Hello", "Ada"), "Hello, Ada!")
    local add3 = partial(function(a, b, c) return a + b + c end, 1, 2)
    check_eq(add3(3), 6)
end)

test("nils stay in place", function()
    local show = partial(function(a, b, c) return tostring(a) .. "," .. tostring(b) .. "," .. tostring(c) end, nil, "x")
    check_eq(show(nil), "nil,x,nil")
    check_eq(show(5), "nil,x,5")
end)
